# Make and model {#sec-dd-make-model}

```{r}
source("R/book.R")
cols <- dict_groups$make_model
cs <- coverage_share(cols)
```

## Overview

DVSA records make and model as free text typed at the test station, so one
model can appear in dozens of spellings. The pipeline matches each make and
model to the names used in DfT's vehicle licensing statistics, so CARS results
can be compared with and joined to the official figures.

- **`make_final`** and **`model_final`** are the cleaned make and DfT
  *generic model* (`FORD`, `FIESTA`). Use these for analysis.
- **`derivative_final`** is the rest of the DVSA model text, such as trim,
  engine or body style (`ZETEC CLIMATE`). It is not standardised.
- **`dft_genmodel`** and **`dft_model`** are the DfT names, for joining to DfT
  tables. `dft_model` is filled only where the DVSA text is exactly one DfT
  model string.
- **`make_method`**, **`model_method`** and **`model_confidence`** record how
  each match was made and how sure it is. Filter on them to test whether a
  result depends on the less certain matches.
- **`make_DVSA`**, **`model_DVSA`** and **`make_DVLA`** are the values as
  supplied, kept for checking.

The matching is summarised in @sec-pipeline and set out in full in the
methodology, [section 4](../../reports/methodology.md#stage-2-make-and-model),
including how makes ([4.2](../../reports/methodology.md#makes)) and models
([4.3](../../reports/methodology.md#models)) are matched and
[how the result compares with the DfT counts](../../reports/methodology.md#comparison-with-the-dft-counts).
The vehicle's body type, found from the matched model, is described with the
other classifications in @sec-dd-vehicle-type.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-make-model
#| tbl-cap: "Make and model columns."
dict_table("make_model")
```

## Coverage

The DVSA make and model are present for almost every vehicle, and the cleaned
make for `r cov_pct(cs, "make_final", digits = 1)`: it is blank only where the
supplied make is a placeholder such as `UNKNOWN`. A generic model is found for
`r cov_pct(cs, "model_final")` of vehicles. Matching is a little weaker for the
oldest vehicles, first used before 2000 (`r cov_pct(cs, "model_final", "Before 2000")`),
more of whose models do not appear in the DfT statistics.

The derivative and the exact DfT model string change most over time
(@fig-dd-make-model). Both depend on how much detail DVSA's model text holds,
and DVSA records much fuller model names for recent vehicles: the derivative
is present for `r cov_year("derivative_final", 2015)` of vehicles first used
in 2015, but `r cov_year("derivative_final", 2024)` of those first used in
2024.

The DVLA make is present wherever a VES record was found, which is rarer for
older vehicles: see @sec-dd-dvla-status.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dd-make-model-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Share of vehicles with a value, by year of first use."
coverage_table(cols)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dd-make-model
#| fig-cap: "Share of vehicles with a value in selected make and model columns, by year of first use."
#| fig-height: 4.6
coverage_plot(c("make_final", "model_final", "derivative_final", "dft_model"))
```

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, by year of first use, from 1990. Numeric columns and
dates show the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper quartile (Q3) and
maximum; other columns show the share of vehicles with each value, with the
less common values grouped as *All other values* and missing values as
*Blank*.

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(dict_values("make_model"))
```
